The color glaze is formulated from a high-temperature resistant white glaze mineral and water. In this formulation, the high-temperature resistant white glaze mineral accounts for 50 wt% to 66 wt% of the color glaze, while water accounts for 34 wt% to 50 wt%.

The white toning glaze contains 70 wt% high-temperature resistant white glaze mineral and 30 wt% water. This component is used to adjust the tone and brightness of the pigment while maintaining resistance to high-temperature firing conditions.

The colorless toning glaze contains 30 wt% high-temperature resistant colorless glaze mineral and 70 wt% water. This component may be used to dilute, adjust, or modify the transparency and application characteristics of the pigment without significantly changing its color.

A high-temperature color glaze painting pigment is provided for use in porcelain plate painting. The pigment is prepared by combining a color glaze, a white toning glaze, and a colorless toning glaze according to specified proportions. Each glaze component is formed from selected mineral raw materials and water, and the components are mixed in ratios suitable for producing stable color, appropriate viscosity, and good adhesion during painting and firing. By adjusting the amount of white toning glaze and colorless toning glaze, the shade, brightness, transparency, and thickness of the pigment can be controlled, allowing the pigment to meet different artistic and production requirements.

The color glaze serves as the main coloring component of the pigment and provides the desired hue after high-temperature firing. The white toning glaze is used to lighten or soften the color, improve coverage, and create layered visual effects. The colorless toning glaze functions as a regulating medium, helping to adjust fluidity, transparency, and glaze texture without significantly changing the basic color. Through proper formulation, the pigment can maintain good color stability at high firing temperatures and can form a durable glazed surface on a porcelain plate.

A method for making porcelain plate paintings using the high-temperature color glaze pigment is also provided. In the method, a porcelain plate body is first prepared and cleaned to remove dust, oil, or other impurities. The formulated pigment is then applied to the surface of the porcelain plate according to a desired pattern or image. The application may be carried out by hand painting, brushing, spraying, printing, screen printing, or other suitable coating techniques. After the pigment has been applied, the porcelain plate is dried and then fired at a high temperature so that the pigment and the porcelain surface fuse together to form a permanent decorative image.

The process is suitable for both artistic creation and industrial production. When used manually, artists can directly paint on porcelain plates, mix colors as needed, and create unique works with rich glaze effects and strong expressive quality. When used in industrial production, the pigment can be standardized and applied through mechanized or semi-mechanized processes, making it possible to produce porcelain plate paintings in larger quantities while maintaining consistent color and quality.

The high-temperature color glaze pigment provides improved flexibility in color adjustment and application. It allows porcelain plate paintings to be produced in different styles, from individualized handmade artworks to repeatable commercial products. Because the pigment is fired at high temperature, the resulting image has good wear resistance, color durability, and integration with the porcelain substrate. Therefore, the formulation and production method expand the practical use of porcelain plate painting, improve production scalability, and support both traditional craftsmanship and modern manufacturing.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it is also one of the most important. As a definite article, “the” helps us point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we may mean any book, but when we say “the book,” we mean a particular one that the speaker and listener can identify.

This simple word gives clarity and precision to communication. It helps organize our thoughts, connect ideas, and guide the reader or listener toward a specific person, place, object, or concept. For example, “the sun,” “the world,” and “the truth” all feel definite and meaningful because “the” directs attention to something known or unique.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” appears constantly in everyday speech and writing. It is a quiet but essential part of English grammar, making sentences smoother and more understandable. Without it, language would feel incomplete, vague, and less natural.

In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can carry great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a high-temperature colored glaze painting pigment, including composition ratios for color glaze, white toning glaze, colorless toning glaze, and its use in porcelain plate painting.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A high-temperature colored glaze painting pigment and a method for using the same in porcelain plate painting are disclosed. The pigment comprises a color glaze, a white toning glaze and a colorless toning glaze, which are respectively prepared from ceramic glaze raw materials and high-temperature stable colorants. The color glaze comprises, by weight, 45–65 parts feldspar, 10–25 parts quartz, 8–18 parts kaolin, 3–10 parts calcined talc or dolomite, 2–8 parts calcium carbonate, 1–5 parts zinc oxide, 0.5–3 parts boron-containing frit, and 3–15 parts high-temperature ceramic colorant. The white toning glaze comprises, by weight, 50–70 parts feldspar, 10–20 parts quartz, 8–18 parts kaolin, 3–8 parts calcium carbonate, 1–5 parts zinc oxide, and 5–15 parts zirconium silicate or tin oxide white opacifier. The colorless toning glaze comprises, by weight, 55–75 parts feldspar, 10–25 parts quartz, 5–15 parts kaolin, 2–8 parts calcium carbonate, 1–5 parts zinc oxide, and 0.5–5 parts frit, and contains no coloring oxide or opacifying agent. In use, the color glaze is mixed with the white toning glaze and/or the colorless toning glaze in a ratio of 1:0.1–5 to adjust hue, chroma, transparency and layering performance, then ground with water or an organic painting medium to form a painting paste. The paste is applied by brush to the surface of a porcelain plate body or a pre-fired glaze layer, dried, and fired at 1180–1350°C in an oxidizing or neutral atmosphere. After firing, the painted pattern is fused with the porcelain glaze surface, forming a bright, wear-resistant, corrosion-resistant and high-temperature-stable colored glaze image suitable for porcelain plate decorative painting.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical description of a high-temperature glaze painting material for porcelain plates that can be used by artists manually or in industrial production, including detailed wt% formulas.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Description: High-Temperature Glaze Painting Material for Porcelain Plates

### 1. Product Concept

This material is a **high-temperature porcelain glaze-painting composition** intended for decorating porcelain plates before final glaze firing or during a dedicated high-fire decoration firing. It is suitable for:

- **Manual application** by brush, sponge, pen, trailing bottle, or airbrush  
- **Industrial application** by screen printing, pad printing, roller coating, spraying, or digital-paste deposition  
- **Food-contact porcelain ware**, provided the fired surface passes applicable leaching, durability, and migration tests

The material consists of a finely milled **ceramic glaze/frit base**, optional **ceramic colorants or stains**, and an **organic or aqueous painting medium** that provides brushability, suspension stability, adhesion, and controlled drying.

The fired decoration forms a **vitreous, chemically durable, glossy to satin glaze layer** that bonds to porcelain bodies or existing compatible glazes at high temperature.

---

## 2. Typical Firing Range

| Parameter | Typical Range |
|---|---:|
| Firing temperature | 1180–1280 °C |
| Preferred porcelain range | 1220–1260 °C |
| Soak time | 10–30 minutes |
| Atmosphere | Oxidation preferred |
| Heating rate | 80–150 °C/h after burnout |
| Recommended burnout hold | 300–600 °C, adequate ventilation |

The material is designed to mature with high-fire porcelain glazes, producing a durable surface that is more permanent than low-fire overglaze enamels.

---

# 3. Dry Powder Formulas

The following formulas are given in **weight percent of dry inorganic solids**.

---

## Formula A: General-Purpose Transparent High-Temperature Painting Glaze

Suitable as a base for colored painting glazes, brushwork, screen-printing pastes, or overglaze-like high-fire decoration.

### Dry Inorganic Composition

| Raw material | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Potash feldspar | 30.0 |
| Soda feldspar or nepheline syenite | 12.0 |
| Silica, 325 mesh | 22.0 |
| Kaolin, washed | 10.0 |
| Wollastonite | 9.0 |
| Calcium carbonate | 4.0 |
| Zinc oxide | 4.0 |
| Boron frit, lead-free | 6.0 |
| Alumina hydrate | 2.0 |
| Bentonite | 1.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Characteristics

- Lead-free and cadmium-free base
- Glossy transparent fired surface
- Good adhesion to porcelain glaze and body
- Suitable for tinting with ceramic stains
- Moderate melt fluidity, suitable for painted decoration without excessive running

---

## Formula B: High-Gloss High-Fire Painting Glaze, More Fluid

For brighter, glassier brush marks and industrial decoration where a smooth glossy fired surface is desired.

| Raw material | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Potash feldspar | 26.0 |
| Nepheline syenite | 18.0 |
| Silica, 325 mesh | 20.0 |
| Kaolin | 8.0 |
| Wollastonite | 10.0 |
| Zinc oxide | 5.0 |
| Boron frit, lead-free | 8.0 |
| Dolomite | 3.0 |
| Bentonite | 1.0 |
| Zirconium silicate, optional clarity stabilizer | 1.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Characteristics

- Higher gloss than Formula A
- Better melt at 1200–1230 °C
- Suitable for screen printing, brushing, and sprayed decorative effects
- Use carefully on vertical surfaces because it is slightly more fluid

---

## Formula C: Satin High-Temperature Painting Glaze

For matte or satin decorative painting on porcelain plates.

| Raw material | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Potash feldspar | 28.0 |
| Silica, 325 mesh | 24.0 |
| Kaolin | 14.0 |
| Wollastonite | 8.0 |
| Dolomite | 8.0 |
| Talc | 5.0 |
| Zinc oxide | 3.0 |
| Lead-free boron frit | 5.0 |
| Alumina hydrate | 4.0 |
| Bentonite | 1.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Characteristics

- Satin to semi-matte fired surface
- Good for subtle painterly decoration
- Less running than high-gloss versions
- Best fired around 1230–1260 °C

---

# 4. Colored Glaze Painting Formulas

Ceramic stains or oxide colorants may be added to the transparent base. For industrial consistency, **encapsulated ceramic stains** are preferred over raw oxides.

The following formulas are expressed as **wt% of total dry inorganic composition**, including the base and colorant.

---

## White High-Fire Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Formula A base powder | 82.0 |
| Zirconium silicate opacifier | 15.0 |
| Tin oxide, optional brightness enhancer | 2.0 |
| Bentonite or Veegum | 1.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Fired appearance

Opaque white, glossy, suitable for line work, highlights, and under-decoration.

---

## Cobalt Blue Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Formula A base powder | 92.0 |
| Cobalt aluminate blue ceramic stain | 7.0 |
| Bentonite or Veegum | 1.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Notes

- Strong color development at porcelain temperatures
- For softer blue, reduce stain to 2–4 wt%
- Raw cobalt oxide may be used at much lower levels, typically 0.5–2 wt%, but stains give better repeatability

---

## Turquoise / Blue-Green Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Formula A base powder | 88.0 |
| Zirconium-vanadium or cobalt-chromite turquoise stain | 10.0 |
| Bentonite or suspension clay | 2.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Notes

- Use stable high-temperature ceramic stains
- Avoid copper carbonate alone for food-contact surfaces unless tested, as copper can affect glaze durability and leaching

---

## Iron Red-Brown High-Fire Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Formula C satin base powder | 85.0 |
| Red iron oxide | 10.0 |

---

## Black High-Temperature Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |

| Formula A base powder | 84.0 |
| Cobalt-free black ceramic stain, spinel type | 14.0 |
| Bentonite or Veegum | 2.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Notes

- For food-contact ware, use a commercially certified food-contact ceramic stain
- Some black stains contain cobalt, chromium, nickel, iron, or manganese; verify regulatory suitability

---

## Green High-Fire Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Formula A base powder | 88.0 |
| Chromium-free green ceramic stain | 10.0 |
| Bentonite | 2.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Notes

- Chromium-bearing greens are common and stable but require compliance review for food-contact products
- Industrial producers should conduct extraction and migration tests after firing

---

# 5. Ready-to-Use Brush Painting Suspension

For hand painting, the dry glaze powder is dispersed in water with a binder, suspending agent, and humectant.

## Formula D: Aqueous Brush Painting Glaze

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Dry glaze/color powder from Formula A–C or colored versions | 65.0 |
| Deionized water | 27.0 |
| Gum arabic solution, 20% solids | 4.0 |
| Propylene glycol | 2.0 |
| Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose, CMC, 3% solution | 1.5 |
| Nonionic wetting agent | 0.2 |
| Defoamer | 0.1 |
| Preservative/biocide suitable for ceramic slips | 0.2 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Properties

| Property | Typical Value |
|---|---:|
| Solids content | 65–70 wt% |
| Viscosity | 1,000–5,000 cP |
| pH | 7.5–9.0 |
| Specific gravity | 1.55–1.75 g/mL |
| Particle size D90 | preferably below 25 µm |

### Use

Apply by brush to bisque-fired porcelain or to compatible unfired/fired glaze surfaces. Allow to dry fully before firing.

---

# 6. Industrial Screen-Printing Paste

For screen printing on porcelain plates, the glaze powder is incorporated into a higher-viscosity medium.

## Formula E: Water-Based Screen-Printing Paste

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Dry glaze/color powder | 72.0 |
| Deionized water | 17.0 |
| Acrylic emulsion binder, 40–50% solids | 5.0 |
| CMC solution, 3% solids | 2.5 |
| Propylene glycol or glycerol | 2.0 |
| Dispersant, sodium polyacrylate type | 0.4 |
| Nonionic wetting agent | 0.3 |
| Defoamer | 0.2 |
| Preservative | 0.2 |
| Rheology modifier, associative thickener or xanthan | 0.4 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Typical Screen-Printing Parameters

| Parameter | Suggested Range |
|---|---:|
| Mesh | 80–180 mesh, depending on image detail |
| Paste viscosity | 8,000–40,000 cP |
| Dry film thickness | 20–80 µm |
| Fired decoration thickness | 10–50 µm |
| Drying temperature | 40–80 °C |
| Firing | 1200–1260 °C |

---

# 7. Industrial Spray or Airbrush Suspension

## Formula F: Sprayable High-Fire Glaze Paint

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Dry glaze/color powder | 55.0 |
| Deionized water | 39.0 |
| Acrylic binder, 40% solids | 2.0 |
| CMC solution, 3% solids | 1.5 |
| Dispersant | 0.4 |
| Wetting agent | 0.2 |
| Propylene glycol | 1.0 |
| Defoamer | 0.1 |
| Preservative | 0.2 |
| Ammonia or pH adjuster, as needed | 0.1 |
| Thickener, as needed | 0.5 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Typical Properties

| Property | Range |
|---|---:|
| Viscosity | 50–500 cP |
| Specific gravity | 1.35–1.55 g/mL |
| Recommended nozzle | 0.5–1.5 mm |
| Wet film thickness | 30–150 µm |

---

# 8. Oil-Based or Solvent-Based Painting Medium

Some artists and factories prefer an oil-based medium for slower drying and smoother brush lines.

## Formula G: Oil-Based Hand-Painting Medium

This formula describes the **medium only**. Mix with dry glaze powder as needed.

| Component | wt% |
|---|---:|
| Lavender oil, pine oil, or high-boiling glycol ether | 45.0 |
| Stand oil or alkyd resin solution | 20.0 |
| Terpineol | 20.0 |
| Ethyl cellulose or similar binder | 5.0 |
| Castor oil derivative rheology additive | 5.0 |
| Dispersant compatible with ceramics | 3.0 |
| Anti-skinning agent or antioxidant | 1.0 |
| Wetting aid | 1.0 |
| **Total** | **100.0** |

### Mixing Ratio

| Component | wt% in finished paint |
|---|---:|
| Dry glaze/color powder | 70–80 |
| Oil-based medium | 20–30 |

This type of medium requires a well-ventilated burnout stage during firing.

---

# 9. Manufacturing Procedure

### Dry Powder Preparation

1. **Weigh raw materials** according to the selected formula.
2. **Blend dry materials** in a ribbon blender, ball mill, or high-shear mixer.
3. **Wet mill** with water to reduce particle size.
4. Target particle size:  
   - Hand painting: D90 below 30 µm  
   - Screen printing: D90 below 15–20 µm  
   - Fine line work: D90 below 10–15 µm
5. Dry the slurry by filter pressing, spray drying, or tray drying.
6. Sieve through 100–200 mesh.
7. Blend with ceramic stain if not co-milled.

### Paste Preparation

1. Prepare the liquid medium separately.
2. Slowly add dry glaze/color powder under agitation.
3. Mix until homogeneous.
4. Pass through a three-roll mill or bead mill for industrial consistency.
5. De-air under vacuum if needed.
6. Adjust viscosity with water, thickener, or additional powder.
7. Package in sealed plastic or metal containers.

---

# 10. Application Methods

## Manual Artist Use

- Stir thoroughly before use.
- Apply to bisque porcelain or glazed porcelain compatible with the firing schedule.
- Use thin, even layers for line work.
- For opaque colors, two coats may be used.
- Allow each coat to dry before applying the next.
- Fire according to glaze maturity, typically 1220–1260 °C.

## Industrial Production

Suitable processes include:

- Screen printing
- Pad printing
- Banding
- Robotic brush application
- Airless or pneumatic spraying
- Decal production using high-fire ceramic inks
- Roller or curtain decoration

Industrial production should control:

- Viscosity
- Specific gravity
- Particle size
- Drying rate
- Fired color
- Fired gloss
- Thermal expansion compatibility

---

# 11. Performance Requirements

A suitable high-temperature glaze painting material for porcelain plates should meet the following targets:

| Property | Recommended Target |
|---|---:|
| Fired adhesion | No flaking or crawling |
| Fired surface | Smooth, vitreous |
| Gloss, glossy type | 70–95 GU at 60° |
| Gloss, satin type | 20–50 GU at 60° |
| Thermal expansion | Compatible with porcelain body/glaze |
| Acid resistance | No visible attack after household acid exposure |
| Dishwasher durability | No significant fading after repeated cycles |
| Food-contact compliance | Must pass relevant migration/leach testing |

---

# 12. Safety and Regulatory Notes

For porcelain plates intended for food use:

- Avoid lead and cadmium compounds unless using certified encapsulated materials and testing confirms compliance.
- Prefer **lead-free, cadmium-free ceramic stains**.
- Verify heavy metal migration after firing according to relevant standards, such as FDA, California Proposition 65, EU 1935/2004, ISO, or local food-contact ceramic regulations.
- Ensure adequate ventilation during firing, especially when organic media are used.
- Provide SDS documentation for industrial users.
- Wear respiratory protection when handling dry ceramic powders, especially silica-containing materials.

---

## Summary

The material is a **lead-free high-temperature glaze painting system** composed of a porcelain-compatible glaze base, ceramic pigments, and an aqueous or oil-based medium. It can be formulated for glossy, satin, transparent, opaque, or colored decoration and applied by both artists and industrial processes. Typical dry glaze compositions contain feldspar, silica, kaolin, calcium/magnesium fluxes, zinc oxide, boron frit, and ceramic stains, with firing in the **1180–1280 °C** range.

**Patent Abstract**

The invention relates to a high-temperature colored glaze painting pigment for porcelain plate painting manufacture. The pigment comprises, by weight, 35–55 parts of ceramic colorant, 20–35 parts of transparent or semi-transparent high-temperature glaze frit, 5–15 parts of kaolin or alumina clay, 3–10 parts of feldspar, 2–8 parts of quartz powder, 1–5 parts of zirconium silicate or tin oxide opacifier, 0.2–2 parts of suspending agent, and 0.1–1 part of dispersing agent. Clean water is added in an amount of 25–45% of the total dry material weight to form a brushable or sprayable glaze-paint slurry. In use, the pigment may be mixed with a base glaze at a ratio of 1:0.5–1:3, preferably 1:1–1:2, according to the desired color strength and transparency. The composition is suitable for firing at 1180–1320°C and forms a stable colored glaze layer integrated with the porcelain surface.

The high-temperature colored glaze painting pigment has good suspension stability, smooth painting performance, high color development, strong adhesion, and excellent resistance to wear, acid, alkali, and fading. The pigment is particularly suitable for hand painting, screen printing, spraying, or decorative glaze application on porcelain plates, enabling clear patterns, durable coloration, reduced cracking and pinholes, and improved production yield in porcelain plate painting manufacture.
